sources.title: Visa Requirements for Foreigners Travelling to The Bahamas
sources.officialityEvidence: The live Bahamas government CDN document is headed as the foreign-visitor requirements table. It has an internal 18 February 2014 update date and does not name South Sudan, so it is recorded only as an insufficiency, not a status source.
sources.supportingExcerpt: VISA REQUIREMENTS FOR FOREIGNERS TRAVELLING TO THE BAHAMAS

sources.title: List of Countries - Visa Required
sources.publisher: Cayman Islands Customs and Border Control
sources.officialityEvidence: The live Cayman Islands government Customs and Border Control table distinguishes named visa-required and visa-not-required countries. It contains Sudan but no separate South Sudan row.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Common Name of Country Official Name of Country Visa Required Unless Exempted Visa Not Required

sources.title: Visas
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Bosnia and Herzegovina
sources.officialityEvidence: The live Ministry visa page identifies the foreign-visitor visa-information service and presents country cards. The new page remains under construction, has an incomplete TLS chain in this environment, and provides no South Sudan card or exact result.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Na ovome mjestu možete dobiti informacije o viznom režimu za građane BiH, kao i za strance

sources.title: Do you need a visa to travel to Belize?
sources.publisher: Ministry of Immigration, Governance and Labour
sources.officialityEvidence: Belize Immigration's live Government table instructs travellers to search their nationality. It has no South Sudan row; its United States, Schengen and Canadian exemptions are explicitly third-country-document conditions.
sources.supportingExcerpt: To search if you qualify for a Visa enter country of nationality to see if you may require visa to Belize.

sources.title: Clasificación de países
sources.officialityEvidence: Guatemala's national migration authority publishes the current visitor-category definitions on its official domain. The page was Cloudflare-blocked during direct review and neither it nor the Foreign Ministry schedule yields a separate South Sudan result.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Los países que se encuentran en la categoría A, no necesitan visa para ingresar al territorio guatemalteco.

sources.title: Nicaragua eAIP GEN 1.3: passenger entry, transit and exit
sources.publisher: Instituto Nicaragüense de Aeronáutica Civil / COCESNA eAIP
sources.officialityEvidence: INAC's official AIP points to the COCESNA-hosted Nicaragua eAIP. Its current visa-category material does not provide a machine-readable, separately selected South Sudan ordinary-passport result.
sources.supportingExcerpt: A: exento de visa; B: consular o sin consulta; C: consultada.

sources.title: MIREX ordinary tourist selector: Republic of South Sudan
sources.officialityEvidence: The live MIREX result selects Republic of South Sudan, ordinary passport and tourist visa, and returns a visa-required answer with consular jurisdiction in Khartoum.

sources.title: Tourist Card: entry requirements and visa-required countries
sources.officialityEvidence: DGII's live official Tourist Card page supplies an express residual rule after a named consular-visa list. South Sudan is absent from that list while the contemporaneous MIREX ordinary-passport result says a visa is required.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Los nacionales de los países que no aparecen en el listado anterior deben ingresar con la Tarjeta de Turista.

conflicts.explanation: The current MIREX ordinary-tourist selector directly says South Sudan requires a visa, matching the fallback, while DGII's explicit residual Tourist Card rule would treat South Sudan as eligible because it is absent from DGII's named visa list. The conflicting official results prevent a stable classification.

unresolved.reason: The live Bahamas visitor table and current legal materials do not name South Sudan; the table also retains a 2014 internal update date. Neither absence nor the Bahamas online application service establishes a South Sudan eVisa, advance-visa or visa-free baseline.

Cayman Customs and Border Control's live nationality table contains Sudan but no distinct South Sudan row. Sudan's result is not transferred, and no visa-required complement is inferred from South Sudan's absence.

Bosnia and Herzegovina's current Ministry page supplies no South Sudan country card or selected ordinary-passport result. Its incomplete new selector and generic consular rules do not establish a nationality-wide advance-visa baseline; document-conditioned Schengen/EU/United States exceptions are excluded.

Belize Immigration's live nationality table has no South Sudan result. Its exemption for holders of specified United States, Schengen or Canadian documents is conditional and cannot establish an ordinary South Sudan passport baseline.

Current Guatemalan materials classify Sudan but do not provide a separate South Sudan ordinary-passport result. The category definitions do not authorize a legacy-name transfer or a residual visa complement.

Nicaragua's official AIP publishes A/B/C visitor-visa categories, but its available country materials do not give a direct, separately readable South Sudan ordinary-passport result. No eVisa status is inferred from online or AIP availability.

The current MIREX ordinary-tourist selector says South Sudan requires a visa, while DGII's explicit residual Tourist Card rule would cover it only by omission. No current primary source reconciles those conflicting ordinary-passport results or establishes a safe issuance baseline.
